item: Row J R153/R154: a restore hands a verdict on to a new sibling feed in the disqualified direction only, and a status held by an inherited verdict keeps its early local re-check
refs: R153; R154; branch claude/v0-5-plan-j8zvre (PR number at push)
summary: The restore-merge's sibling rule (R148, R150) is narrowed by ruling to the safe direction: if any measured local feed of the outlet is disqualified, the unmatched incoming feed lands disqualified with an inherited attempt; under a qualified outlet nothing is handed on, so the feed keeps its own incoming evidence (unjudged stays unjudged and gets its own trial, disqualified stays disqualified, qualified keeps what the other instance measured on that very feed) and is reported with the rule 'no feed of the outlet is disqualified (a qualified verdict is not handed on)'. That also removes the case the Opus read found where a qualified outlet laundered a disqualified feed into collection. The boot step that lists inversions for an early local re-check now lists every status held by an inherited verdict as well (repair_inversions reports them as held_by_inherited_verdict_rows), so the install measures them itself rather than waiting a whole interval after the other instance's attempt.
